image_description: A close-up, side-view of a male duck (drake) floating on water. The image focuses on the rear half of the bird's body, showing detailed plumage textures, the characteristic curled tail feathers, and the blue speculum patch on the wing. The head is partially visible on the far left but mostly out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head and bill are largely outside the frame or obscured by the angle; only the back of the neck/head area is visible.
The eye is not visible in this cropped composition focusing on the body and tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows dense, layered feather textures consistent with waterproof plumage. The buoyancy is evident from the waterline interaction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plumage displays complex patterns with brown speckling, grey flanks, and distinct black/white/blue markings on the tail/wing area, consistent with male duck breeding plumage (specifically resembling a Mallard or similar dabbling duck).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are submerged and not visible in the image.
The folded wing structure is visible along the side, showing the characteristic layering and the blue speculum patch bordered by white stripes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central tail feathers are clearly visible curling upwards, a definitive anatomical feature of drakes.

artifact_observations.location: Water surface near the bottom right corner
artifact_observations.reasoning: The water ripples in the foreground appear slightly smudged and lack the sharp specular highlights seen elsewhere, suggesting minor generative smoothing or inconsistency in fluid dynamics simulation.
